title: withdrawPSM takes a maximum rather than an exact amount and charges the rate limit against what was actually withdrawn
content:
The two PSM functions on the `ForeignController` differ in a way that is easy to miss. A...3.3.1.1 declares `depositPSM(address asset, uint256 amount)` with the limit applied declaratively as a modifier, `rateLimitedAsset(LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT, asset, amount)` — an exact amount, metered before the body runs.

A...3.3.1.2 declares `withdrawPSM(address asset, uint256 maxAmount)` and describes it as withdrawing "**up to** `maxAmount` of `asset` from the PSM to the ALM Proxy, returning the amount actually withdrawn as `assetsWithdrawn`. The withdrawn amount is then applied against the `LIMIT_PSM_WITHDRAW` rate limit for the asset."

The asymmetry follows from which side controls feasibility. A deposit's size is entirely Grove's choice, so an exact amount is meaningful and pre-charging is correct. A withdrawal is bounded by whatever liquidity the PSM currently holds, so demanding an exact amount would convert normal liquidity variation into reverts — and reverts are worst precisely when exiting matters most.

The accompanying accounting consequence is that a best-effort withdrawal must be metered post-hoc, which is why the limit cannot be expressed as a modifier here. The signature shape and the charge point are two views of the same fact: the caller does not know the outcome in advance.
description: Best-effort withdrawal means thin PSM liquidity yields a partial fill instead of a revert, in contrast to depositPSM which charges LIMIT_PSM_DEPOSIT up front via a modifier.
